blocks.text: The headline finding: Headroom indicted its own architecture

content.value: “Headroom is built on the wrong mental model: compression means choosing what to drop from conversation history.” — REALIGNMENT/00-overview.md, in Headroom's own repo
The flagship compressor ships with a 3,900-line, 14-file self-audit (
REALIGNMENT/
) in which ten parallel audit subagents found 5 P0 “cache-killer” bugs affecting every customer and retired roughly 25K lines of code. The corrected mental model they converged on —

children.value: passthrough is sacred; compress only the live zone; hash-keyed; position-preserving

content.value: — is a proxy painfully rediscovering what a system of record has by construction.

a CMS that renders brief views AT THE SOURCE has no proxy seam to violate. Tool output that is born brief cannot corrupt a stream it never rewrites, cannot bust a provider cache it never sits in front of, and cannot lose data behind a marker whose store it IS. The 61k-star project's own conclusion is that its proxy mutations were the bug.

blocks.caption: Two architectures. Headroom mutates traffic in flight and parks originals in a TTL side-store; Barkpark renders brief at the source and the handle points into the system of record itself.

items.label: L1
items.text: Totals and truncation markers ride IN the same payload, never in side-band metadata an adapter can drop. Proof: #2421's complete-looking outline with 26 silently missing definitions. Already AXI law 2 — this issue is why it can never be relaxed.

items.label: L2
items.text: A miss must say 'gone — do not retry; re-fetch the source' in words a model follows. Proof: #1776's agent retried one dead hash 25× in 11 minutes. Keep a retrieval round/dedup budget even with infinite TTL.

items.label: L3
items.lead: Agent-facing output is deterministic and stably ordered.
items.text: Same input, same bytes; volatile values stripped or at the tail; tool sets session-sticky (REALIGNMENT I4/I7, cross-cutting #8). Cache writes are 58.8% of fleet cost — prefix stability is where the money is. A detector/lint is safe; a rewriter is proven harmful.

items.label: L4
items.text: Any brief or compacted view keeps error/blocked items unconditionally (SmartCrusher's one universally sound constraint, planning.rs). Open placement question: brief task views vs bp park only — it changes the frozen AXI card contract.

items.label: L5
items.lead: Feedback observes; it never adapts per-request.
items.text: Usage signals become censuses published between releases, never inputs to the same request's rendering (REALIGNMENT I9; TOIN demoted to observation-only because per-request adaptation makes identical inputs nondeterministic — which violates L3).

content.value: Per-request compression is real in Headroom's home regime, but nobody — vendor or independent — has ever demonstrated a net win on an Anthropic cache-priced rail, and the one rigorous study found lighter-but-more turns netting HIGHER bills with the mechanism unresolved. Design the duel expecting ≈0 savings plus cache regression, and pre-register the kill criterion.

content.value: Headroom's failures are a proxy's failures. The trap is deriving smugness instead of laws: Barkpark can still violate L1–L5 natively (a brief view that hides errors, a census that feeds back per-request, a search payload that busts caches) — being the system of record removes the seam, not the responsibility. Every law therefore ships with a per-emitter acceptance criterion.

Headroom Strip-Mined: Verdicts, Laws, and Horror Stories for the ctx-compression Epic

Deep investigation · 2026-07-23 · Lane: headroom-lessons · Capstone: ctx-compression-capstone

This paper owns the external evidence for the Barkpark context-compression epic. Headroom (github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom, Apache-2.0) was cloned and read at algorithm level, all 256 open issues were censused one by one, its 14-file REALIGNMENT self-audit was digested invariant by invariant, and the only independent benchmark in existence was chased to its source. Every mechanism gets a verdict — ADOPT NATIVELY, REJECT, or TEST FIRST — with citations to specific code and issues. Done means a future strategist never needs to open the Headroom repo.

The headline finding: Headroom indicted its own architecture

“Headroom is built on the wrong mental model: compression means choosing what to drop from conversation history.” — REALIGNMENT/00-overview.md, in Headroom's own repo

The flagship compressor ships with a 3,900-line, 14-file self-audit (REALIGNMENT/) in which ten parallel audit subagents found 5 P0 “cache-killer” bugs affecting every customer and retired roughly 25K lines of code. The corrected mental model they converged on — passthrough is sacred; compress only the live zone; hash-keyed; position-preserving — is a proxy painfully rediscovering what a system of record has by construction.

The punchline for Barkpark: a CMS that renders brief views AT THE SOURCE has no proxy seam to violate. Tool output that is born brief cannot corrupt a stream it never rewrites, cannot bust a provider cache it never sits in front of, and cannot lose data behind a marker whose store it IS. The 61k-star project's own conclusion is that its proxy mutations were the bug.

One residual worth keeping on the shelf: on foreign bulk — payloads Barkpark does not own the schema for (the future bp park ingest) — a tiny deterministic SmartCrusher subset (dedup, first/last anchors, always-keep-errors, count-honest elision) is defensible, because guessing is all anyone has there. The cross-lane spend census refuted the whale premise (≥10KB results are only 14.6% of fleet bytes), so this ships as a defer-by-default recipe documented for when foreign bulk actually arrives — not a wave-1 build.

NATIVE-ONLY: confirmed, overwhelming
The interview's stance survives contact with all evidence classes at once. (a) Supply chain: transitive dep ast-grep-cli 0.44.1 TROJANED; the exclusion merged but the 0.32.1 PyPI wheel shipped without it — fresh installs still resolve the trojaned build today (#2462, #2267). (b) Economics: 2–7× measured cost increase, tokens_saved 0.00% across seven matched Claude Code runs (#2438). (c) Reliability: discarded completed paid responses + 502 retries drove a 5-hour org quota 2%→97% in 15 minutes; one 420K-token record counted 19×; proxy remained active after unwrap (#2340). (d) Protocol: signed thinking blocks corrupted → 400 (#2251); injected system message → 400 (#765). (e) Silent no-ops are the largest invisible-failure class in the tracker (18 open issues). (f) The client fights back: Claude Code ≥2.1.196 gates remote control to api.anthropic.com (#1779). No Headroom runtime near keys or prod — ever.

The five laws Headroom proves

The issue tracker is a complete failure taxonomy of guess-based compression over an ephemeral store. The store-fragility half (TTL cliffs, restart wipes, empty stores, markers outliving entries) is structurally eliminated by the handle doctrine — no law needed, the architecture is the law. The presentation half must be adopted explicitly. Each law below is priced by measured failure frequency in the census.

L1Completeness lives in-payload. Totals and truncation markers ride IN the same payload, never in side-band metadata an adapter can drop. Proof: #2421's complete-looking outline with 26 silently missing definitions. Already AXI law 2 — this issue is why it can never be relaxed.
L2Dead handles fail terminally, imperatively. A miss must say 'gone — do not retry; re-fetch the source' in words a model follows. Proof: #1776's agent retried one dead hash 25× in 11 minutes. Keep a retrieval round/dedup budget even with infinite TTL.
L3Agent-facing output is deterministic and stably ordered. Same input, same bytes; volatile values stripped or at the tail; tool sets session-sticky (REALIGNMENT I4/I7, cross-cutting #8). Cache writes are 58.8% of fleet cost — prefix stability is where the money is. A detector/lint is safe; a rewriter is proven harmful.
L4Errors are never elided. Any brief or compacted view keeps error/blocked items unconditionally (SmartCrusher's one universally sound constraint, planning.rs). Open placement question: brief task views vs bp park only — it changes the frozen AXI card contract.
L5Feedback observes; it never adapts per-request. Usage signals become censuses published between releases, never inputs to the same request's rendering (REALIGNMENT I9; TOIN demoted to observation-only because per-request adaptation makes identical inputs nondeterministic — which violates L3).

Good news on L3: the determinism probe found bp already mostly compliant — see the measured section below. The remaining work is two volatile search fields and a lint, not a rebuild.

What we will create

This lane builds no code. Its deliverables are the parts of the epic charter that must never be re-litigated:

  1. The verdict table, frozen. REJECT all proxy/wrap production paths; ADOPT handles-as-CMS, cache-invariant-as-lint, learn-as-native-failure-mining; TEST FIRST the tabular duel. Citations travel with the verdicts so nobody re-opens the repo to check.
  2. The five laws as charter laws — each with an acceptance criterion phrased per emitter (brief views, park receipts, MCP lists), so builders inherit testable obligations, not vibes.
  3. The audit-wrap cage spec (below), attached to the open duel task task-1e7f85dc19f71e00 so a Sonnet can run it mechanically — or the user can close it on external evidence.
  4. Calibrated savings priors handed to the serialization-experiment lane: expect ~5–8% per-request in Headroom's own regime, ≈0 on Claude Code traffic, 86–100% only on JSON dict-arrays ≥5 items ≥200 tokens.
  5. The foreign-bulk compaction recipe, defer-by-default, for a future bp park — the one regime where deterministic guessing is legitimate.
TEST FIRST: the duel this lane demands
Deterministic tabular/brief render profile vs stats-crush, on bp's own payloads. Headroom's own evolution predicts the outcome: they added a LOSSLESS-first csv-schema stage and gave it a LOWER savings bar (15%) than the lossy path, explicitly because lossless output needs no retrieval round-trip. On declared-schema data, the deterministic profile should win outright.
Ruling this lane does NOT make
Whether the brief card carries rev (the handle anchor) is a three-lane convergence — view-tiers-seam froze the card without rev, handle-doctrine needs rev on it, taskboard-flagship wants it on every board card. The capstone (ctx-compression-capstone) owns that ruling; this paper only supplies the external evidence that rev-anchored handles kill the store-fragility class.

The audit-mode wrap: cage spec

The wrap stays a disposable local measuring instrument (interview Q3). It may exist for exactly one duel, in exactly this cage — and issue #2340 ('remains active after unwrap') is why removal is proven by file diff, never by the tool's own doctor.

Top risk: fighting the last war
Headroom's failures are a proxy's failures. The trap is deriving smugness instead of laws: Barkpark can still violate L1–L5 natively (a brief view that hides errors, a census that feeds back per-request, a search payload that busts caches) — being the system of record removes the seam, not the responsibility. Every law therefore ships with a per-emitter acceptance criterion.

Judgment calls explicitly left to the user:

The headline finding: Headroom indicted its own architecture

“Headroom is built on the wrong mental model: compression means choosing what to drop from conversation history.” — REALIGNMENT/00-overview.md, in Headroom's own repo

The flagship compressor ships with a 3,900-line, 14-file self-audit (REALIGNMENT/) in which ten parallel audit subagents found 5 P0 “cache-killer” bugs affecting every customer and retired roughly 25K lines of code. The corrected mental model they converged on — passthrough is sacred; compress only the live zone; hash-keyed; position-preserving — is a proxy painfully rediscovering what a system of record has by construction.

The punchline for Barkpark: a CMS that renders brief views AT THE SOURCE has no proxy seam to violate. Tool output that is born brief cannot corrupt a stream it never rewrites, cannot bust a provider cache it never sits in front of, and cannot lose data behind a marker whose store it IS. The 61k-star project's own conclusion is that its proxy mutations were the bug.

NATIVE-ONLY: confirmed, overwhelming The interview's stance survives contact with all evidence classes at once. (a) Supply chain: transitive dep ast-grep-cli 0.44.1 TROJANED; the exclusion merged but the 0.32.1 PyPI wheel shipped without it — fresh installs still resolve the trojaned build today (#2462, #2267). (b) Economics: 2–7× measured cost increase, tokens_saved 0.00% across seven matched Claude Code runs (#2438). (c) Reliability: discarded completed paid responses + 502 retries drove a 5-hour org quota 2%→97% in 15 minutes; one 420K-token record counted 19×; proxy remained active after unwrap (#2340). (d) Protocol: signed thinking blocks corrupted → 400 (#2251); injected system message → 400 (#765). (e) Silent no-ops are the largest invisible-failure class in the tracker (18 open issues). (f) The client fights back: Claude Code ≥2.1.196 gates remote control to api.anthropic.com (#1779). No Headroom runtime near keys or prod — ever.

The five laws Headroom proves

The issue tracker is a complete failure taxonomy of guess-based compression over an ephemeral store. The store-fragility half (TTL cliffs, restart wipes, empty stores, markers outliving entries) is structurally eliminated by the handle doctrine — no law needed, the architecture is the law. The presentation half must be adopted explicitly. Each law below is priced by measured failure frequency in the census.

L1
Completeness lives in-payload. Totals and truncation markers ride IN the same payload, never in side-band metadata an adapter can drop. Proof: #2421's complete-looking outline with 26 silently missing definitions. Already AXI law 2 — this issue is why it can never be relaxed.
L2
Dead handles fail terminally, imperatively. A miss must say 'gone — do not retry; re-fetch the source' in words a model follows. Proof: #1776's agent retried one dead hash 25× in 11 minutes. Keep a retrieval round/dedup budget even with infinite TTL.
L3
Agent-facing output is deterministic and stably ordered. Same input, same bytes; volatile values stripped or at the tail; tool sets session-sticky (REALIGNMENT I4/I7, cross-cutting #8). Cache writes are 58.8% of fleet cost — prefix stability is where the money is. A detector/lint is safe; a rewriter is proven harmful.
L4
Errors are never elided. Any brief or compacted view keeps error/blocked items unconditionally (SmartCrusher's one universally sound constraint, planning.rs). Open placement question: brief task views vs bp park only — it changes the frozen AXI card contract.
L5
Feedback observes; it never adapts per-request. Usage signals become censuses published between releases, never inputs to the same request's rendering (REALIGNMENT I9; TOIN demoted to observation-only because per-request adaptation makes identical inputs nondeterministic — which violates L3).

Good news on L3: the determinism probe found bp already mostly compliant — see the measured section below. The remaining work is two volatile search fields and a lint, not a rebuild.

What we will create

This lane builds no code. Its deliverables are the parts of the epic charter that must never be re-litigated:

  1. The verdict table, frozen. REJECT all proxy/wrap production paths; ADOPT handles-as-CMS, cache-invariant-as-lint, learn-as-native-failure-mining; TEST FIRST the tabular duel. Citations travel with the verdicts so nobody re-opens the repo to check.
  2. The five laws as charter laws — each with an acceptance criterion phrased per emitter (brief views, park receipts, MCP lists), so builders inherit testable obligations, not vibes.
  3. The audit-wrap cage spec (below), attached to the open duel task task-1e7f85dc19f71e00 so a Sonnet can run it mechanically — or the user can close it on external evidence.
  4. Calibrated savings priors handed to the serialization-experiment lane: expect ~5–8% per-request in Headroom's own regime, ≈0 on Claude Code traffic, 86–100% only on JSON dict-arrays ≥5 items ≥200 tokens.
  5. The foreign-bulk compaction recipe, defer-by-default, for a future bp park — the one regime where deterministic guessing is legitimate.
TEST FIRST: the duel this lane demands
Deterministic tabular/brief render profile vs stats-crush, on bp's own payloads. Headroom's own evolution predicts the outcome: they added a LOSSLESS-first csv-schema stage and gave it a LOWER savings bar (15%) than the lossy path, explicitly because lossless output needs no retrieval round-trip. On declared-schema data, the deterministic profile should win outright.
Ruling this lane does NOT make
Whether the brief card carries rev (the handle anchor) is a three-lane convergence — view-tiers-seam froze the card without rev, handle-doctrine needs rev on it, taskboard-flagship wants it on every board card. The capstone (ctx-compression-capstone) owns that ruling; this paper only supplies the external evidence that rev-anchored handles kill the store-fragility class.

Risks and unknowns

Top risk: fighting the last war Headroom's failures are a proxy's failures. The trap is deriving smugness instead of laws: Barkpark can still violate L1–L5 natively (a brief view that hides errors, a census that feeds back per-request, a search payload that busts caches) — being the system of record removes the seam, not the responsibility. Every law therefore ships with a per-emitter acceptance criterion.

Judgment calls explicitly left to the user:

  1. Run or close the audit duel. #2438 already measured tokens_saved 0.00% + cache regression on Claude Code traffic; the prior paper's ≥15% wrap gate is almost certainly unreachable. Realistic value of running: a cheap, pre-registered REJECT confirmation on our own receipts that closes the wrap question forever. Cost: an afternoon inside the cage spec.
  2. Always-keep-errors placement. Server-side in brief views (amends the frozen AXI card, strongest guarantee) vs bp park foreign-bulk only (zero contract churn). This lane leans server-side; the card-contract owner should rule.
  3. Threshold policy for censuses. Any alarm number ('brief-view escapes >N% → view too thin') is exactly as folkloric as Headroom's 0.5/0.8 until measured. Options: charter forbids numeric thresholds until a census exists, or accepts provisional folklore with a review date.
  4. Upstream positioning. A Barkpark storage backend for Headroom's CCR store (prior paper path 5) is evidentially toxic short-term (supply chain, realignment churn) — but the positioning value is strategic taste, not evidence. Default: no.

Known unknowns: whether tokbench's proposed R2 (cache-priced Anthropic rail) ever ran — nobody has measured Headroom on the rail Barkpark actually pays for; whether a plain wrap claude can reach the launchd persistence path without --persistent (needs a runtime trace before the cage spec declares launchd out of scope); and Headroom moves fast — every citation here is pinned to the 2026-07-23 clone.
